native_result.query: Between which two races is the factor of BA degree completion -0.9568 when compared to the other?
native_result.HypoA: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.
native_result.HypoB: The factor -0.9568 is the coefficient on the Black race dummy in a logistic regression of BA DEGREE COMPLETED on race with White as the omitted reference category, on the log-odds scale. It therefore arises between Black and White respondents: Black respondents carry -0.9568 relative to White, i.e. exp(-0.9568)=0.384, about 62% lower odds of completing a BA than White respondents (implied probability 0.0139 vs 0.0354). The unpenalised MLE value on this file is -1.005703 (SE 0.2042, 95% CI -1.4058 to -0.6056); -0.9568 lies inside that CI, and the closest fit is the L2-penalised race-only model (Black = -0.961397). The Hispanic-vs-White coefficient (-0.924136) is excluded because -0.9568 is outside the range the Hispanic coefficient can attain under any adjustment or penalty strength.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Input inspection (8,773 rows, 0 missing, White 5,337 / Black 2,113 / Hispanic 1,323; completion 3.54% / 1.33% / 1.44%). 2) Pre-declared ladder (a) race only through (e) fully adjusted, logit MLE, White=omitted reference, plus LPM/probit/cloglog robustness rows and Black-/Hispanic-referenced falsification fits. 3) Complete non-cherry-picked 2^5 covariate-subset enumeration (62 coefficients, all printed). 4) Attainability-range analysis, Firth and Bayesian MAP rare-event conventions, L2 penalty sweep with bisection. 5) Three-optimiser confirmation, scale-invariance check, bootstrap. 6) Final candidate table with SEs, CIs and z/p against the target. All scripts run via analysis/run_all.py.
